name: Structure a contract and find check points
description: Outline a contract, explain its clauses in plain language and collect points for a professional review.
input:
SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – an entirely fictional contract, for trying things out only.

Software service agreement between Example Cloud GmbH (provider) and Sample Trading KG (customer)

§ 1 Subject: The provider makes the software "ShopPilot" available to the customer as a cloud service and operates it.
§ 2 Term: The agreement starts on 1 April 2026 and runs for 24 months. It renews automatically for 12 months each
time unless it is terminated in writing 6 months before expiry.
§ 3 Fees: EUR 1,200 net per month, payable annually in advance. The provider may adjust prices once a year at
its reasonable discretion.
§ 4 Availability: The provider aims for an availability of 99 % on a monthly average. Maintenance windows do not count.
§ 5 Liability: The provider's liability is limited to three months' fees, except in cases of intent.
§ 6 Data: The provider processes customer data on behalf of the customer. Subcontractors may be used without
prior notice. After the end of the agreement, data is deleted after 30 days.
§ 7 Termination for cause: If payment is more than 14 days late, the provider may block access.
§ 8 Place of jurisdiction: the provider's registered office.

guide.problem: Contracts are long, and important clauses hide in the details. Whether a clause is acceptable also depends on the company's own standards. The workflow outlines a contract, explains it in plain language and checks it against the customer's contract playbook, so that a qualified person sees at once where it deviates. It does not replace legal advice.
guide.flow: The structurer captures parties, term, services and deadlines. Building on this, the clause explainer (plain language) and the check-point analyst work in parallel; both read the contract themselves, as text or as an uploaded file. The check-point analyst searches the company's contract playbook for every clause, cites the playbook section and rates the clause as standard, fallback, deviation or red line. If a red line or another critical clause is found, a decision node adds an in-depth review of these clauses. The report agent combines everything into a structured overview with questions for legal advice.
guide.input: The contract as a file (PDF, Word, Markdown or text) in the field “Contract as a file” or as text, ideally with section numbers. Upload the file directly when you start; the contract does not belong in the knowledge collection. The playbook comes from the knowledge collection; the fictional playbook of Sample Trading KG is included. The sample file contains the fictional contract of the test task.
guide.result: A structured overview with summary, key data, explained clauses, check points and questions for a lawyer, also as a PDF and as an editable Word file. Each check point names the playbook section it was measured against, and topics the playbook does not cover are marked as such. The structurer proposes the key data of the contract for knowledge, for example for a contract register; only what you confirm is stored. The result is a working aid and not legal advice.
guide.adapt: Upload your contract as a file when you start or paste it in. Replace the fictional playbook in the knowledge collection with your own, ideally with the same structure per topic: standard position, acceptable fallback and red line. Topics that matter to you, such as insurance or audit rights, only need to be added to the playbook; the check-point analyst finds them by search.
guide.control: Automatic: the check-point analyst rates every clause against the playbook and counts the critical ones; every red line counts as critical. If the count is above zero, the decision node adds the in-depth review of the critical clauses, otherwise it is skipped. No step waits for a person, and the workflow sends nothing. The overview and its questions are the basis for review by a lawyer; the people involved decide what is negotiated.
guide.why: Explaining and checking are independent of each other and therefore run in parallel on the structure. The playbook is searchable knowledge instead of text in the prompt: legal maintains it in one place, the search brings only the relevant section, and the citation makes every rating traceable. The in-depth review is a branch because it is only worth its cost when a red line is crossed. An orchestrator was not used, because every contract needs the same steps.

structure.name: Contract structurer
structure.description: Records parties, subject, term, fees and deadlines.
structure.system: You structure contracts. Record the parties, subject matter, term and renewal, notice periods, fees and payment terms, service commitments, liability, data protection and place of jurisdiction. Give each item with its location in the contract and note what the contract does not cover.

explain.name: Clause explainer
explain.description: Explains each clause in plain language.
explain.system: You explain contracts to people without legal training. Explain each clause in one to three sentences of plain language: what it governs and what it means in practice for the customer, with a short example where it helps. Do not judge whether a clause is valid.

checkpoints.name: Check-point analyst
checkpoints.description: Checks every clause against the customer's contract playbook and finds unusual, one-sided or missing provisions.
checkpoints.system: You prepare contracts for legal review on behalf of the customer, using the customer's contract playbook. For every clause and for every playbook topic, search the playbook with the search tool. For each check point, cite the playbook section (for example “Playbook P4”), compare the clause with the standard position, the acceptable fallback and the red line, and rate it: meets the standard, within the fallback, deviation beyond the fallback, or red line. A clause that crosses a red line is always critical. Also check the playbook topics the contract does not regulate at all and list them as missing provisions. Where the playbook is silent on a clause, say so explicitly (“The playbook says nothing about this”) and assess the clause only as a general check point, for example automatic renewal, unilateral price changes, weak service commitments, liability caps, subcontractors or data return. If the contract is not one where the playbook's company is the customer, say that the playbook can only serve as a comparison. Explain for each point why it should be checked and phrase a question about it. Do not make a final legal assessment. For each check point, quote the wording of the clause concerned with its reference, so that later steps can work with it without the original document.

fields.points: Check points with playbook section, rating (standard, fallback, deviation, red line or playbook silent), reason and question
fields.critical_count: Number of critical clauses: every clause that crosses a red line of the playbook, and where the playbook is silent, clearly critical clauses (e.g. unlimited or very low liability, data processing without an agreement)

report.name: Contract overview
report.description: Combines explanations and check points into a structured overview.
report.system: You summarise contract analyses for decision-makers. Create a structured overview from the explanations and check points without adding new legal assessments. Phrase the questions so that a lawyer can answer them directly.

fields.overview: Summary of the contract in three to five sentences
fields.key_terms: Key terms with location (term, deadlines, fees)

critical.name: Critical clauses
critical.description: Examines critical clauses in depth and prepares negotiation questions.
critical.system: You prepare contract negotiations. Examine every critical clause in depth: what it means in practice, the worst realistic case, how such clauses are usually worded in comparable contracts and which alternative wording could be proposed. Formulate questions for legal counsel. Do not give a final legal assessment.

contract_file.label: Contract as a file
contract_file.description: Optional: the contract as PDF, Word (DOCX), Markdown or text, at most 20 MB. Simply upload the file here; no knowledge collection is needed. Without a file, the contract text below applies.

SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – an entirely fictional contract, for trying things out only.

Maintenance contract between Example Technology Ltd. (contractor) and Sample Practice LLP (client)

§ 1 Subject: Maintenance of two air-conditioning units in the practice building every six months.
§ 2 Term: 12 months from 1 May 2026; after that, terminable at any time with one month's notice to the end of a month.
§ 3 Fees: EUR 380 net per maintenance visit, due 14 days after invoice. Price changes only with the consent of both parties.
§ 4 Faults: response within 2 working days; spare parts only after prior approval by the client.
§ 5 Liability: in accordance with the statutory provisions.
§ 6 Data protection: no personal data is processed.

playbook.name: Contract_playbook_Sample_Trading
playbook.description: Fictional contract playbook of Sample Trading KG for software and cloud contracts: standard position, fallback and red line per topic.
playbook.content:
# Contract playbook of Sample Trading KG – software and cloud services (fictional)

SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – entirely fictional, for trying things out only.

Version January 2026, owner: purchasing and legal. Applies to contracts in which Sample Trading KG buys software or cloud services as the customer. For each topic: **standard** (what we propose), **fallback** (what we accept without escalation) and **red line** (only with the approval of management and external legal counsel).

## P1 Liability

- **Standard:** unlimited liability for intent, gross negligence, injury to life, body or health and breaches of data protection; otherwise a cap of at least the annual fees.
- **Fallback:** for simple negligence a cap of at least the annual fees, but at least EUR 50,000; for data protection breaches at least twice the annual fees.
- **Red line:** a cap below six months' fees, or liability only for intent (exclusion of gross negligence).

## P2 Term and automatic renewal

- **Standard:** initial term of at most 12 months, then open-ended with a notice period of at most 3 months.
- **Fallback:** initial term of up to 24 months; automatic renewal by at most 12 months, if the notice period is at most 3 months.
- **Red line:** initial term over 36 months, or automatic renewal with a notice period of more than 3 months.

## P3 Notice periods, termination and blocking

- **Standard:** notice in text form (e.g. email) is sufficient. The provider may only block access after a written reminder with a grace period of at least 14 days, and never for disputed invoices.
- **Fallback:** written form, if the provider confirms receipt within 5 working days; blocking after 30 days of payment delay with prior warning.
- **Red line:** blocking access without prior warning, or a special termination right for the provider without good cause.

## P4 Price changes

- **Standard:** fixed prices for the initial term; after that at most one adjustment per year, at most 3 % or according to an agreed index, announced 3 months in advance, with a special termination right.
- **Fallback:** up to 5 % per year with a special termination right.
- **Red line:** unilateral price changes at the provider's discretion without a cap or without a special termination right.

## P5 Availability and service levels (SLA)

- **Standard:** guaranteed availability of 99.5 % per month at the transfer point; maintenance windows of at most 4 hours per month, announced 5 working days in advance, outside our business hours (Mon–Sat 7 am–8 pm); service credits of 5 % of the monthly fee per 0.5 % shortfall; response to critical faults within 4 hours.
- **Fallback:** 99.0 %, if maintenance windows are limited to 4 hours per month and service credits apply.
- **Red line:** availability only as a non-binding target without consequences, or maintenance windows without limit.

## P6 Data processing agreement and subprocessors

- **Standard:** a separate data processing agreement (Art. 28 GDPR) signed before go-live; list of subprocessors as an annex; new subprocessors announced at least 30 days in advance with a right to object; processing only in the EU/EEA.
- **Fallback:** announcement 14 days in advance with a special termination right; countries outside the EU/EEA only with an adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses.
- **Red line:** no data processing agreement, or new subprocessors without prior notice and without a right to object.

## P7 Data return and deletion

- **Standard:** export of all data free of charge in a common machine-readable format (CSV or JSON) at any time and up to 60 days after the end of the contract; deletion only after we confirm the export; deletion confirmed in writing.
- **Fallback:** an export window of 30 days, if the provider announces the deletion 14 days in advance.
- **Red line:** deletion without a prior export option.

## P8 Place of jurisdiction and applicable law

- **Standard:** place of jurisdiction at our registered office; the law of our country applies, excluding the UN Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods.
- **Fallback:** place of jurisdiction at the provider's registered office, if it is in the same country and the same law applies.
- **Red line:** a place of jurisdiction abroad or foreign law.

## Not covered by this playbook

Payment terms, intellectual property and insurance are handled by finance and legal case by case; the playbook contains no positions on them.
